column1: # Behaviours that depend on a cargo feature reaching a crate on every target.
# One row per behaviour. Cargo resolves features per build AND per target, so a
# feature that arrives only through a target-gated dependency silently disappears
# where that dependency does. Nothing in the code or the compiler shows it: the
# crate builds the same source against a dependency with different capabilities.
# Columns: crate, dependency, feature, comma-separated targets, why.
# `scripts/ci/check-load-bearing-features.py` fails when the feature is missing on
# a listed target, when a listed target is not installed, and when a row stops
# meaning anything. It does not compare whole trees: 58 legitimate target-specific
# feature differences exist on the current tree (nix's per-OS lists, tokio's
# windows-sys, the feature sets of platform-only dependencies), and a gate that
# reports those is a gate that gets silenced.
# Add a row the moment a behaviour is found to depend on a feature. Keep the row
# after the crate declares the feature itself: the declaration is the thing that
# can be dropped by the next person tidying Cargo.toml.

column5: MCP elicitation forms are built by walking a JSON Schema properties object; without preserve_order serde_json stores members in a BTreeMap and every form renders alphabetically (the Windows CI leg reported ["alpha", "zeta"] for a schema declared as zeta, alpha)
